subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 26-year-old man is evaluated for recurrent episodes of burning pain in the hands and feet that began in adolescence and are triggered by heat and exercise. Examination shows small, dark red, nonblanching papules clustered around the umbilicus and over the buttocks, and he reports that he rarely sweats. Urinalysis shows 2+ protein, and he has had proteinuria for 3 years. His maternal uncle required dialysis at age 45.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible?
explanation_correct: This patient has the classic early triad of Fabry disease: episodic peripheral neuropathy (acroparesthesias), angiokeratomas, and hypohidrosis, followed by progressive renal failure and cardiovascular disease. Deficient α-galactosidase A leads to accumulation of ceramide trihexoside (globotriaosylceramide) in vascular endothelial cells, podocytes, and neurons. Fabry disease is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern, consistent with the affected maternal uncle. Treatment is recombinant α-galactosidase.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease, with developmental regression and a cherry-red spot in infancy rather than acroparesthesias and angiokeratomas.
explanation_incorrect.B: Arylsulfatase A deficiency causes metachromatic leukodystrophy, a demyelinating disease presenting with ataxia and dementia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Glucocerebrosidase deficiency causes Gaucher disease, with hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, and bone crises.
explanation_incorrect.E: Sphingomyelinase deficiency causes Niemann-Pick disease, with hepatosplenomegaly and a cherry-red spot.

educationalObjective: Angiokeratomas, acroparesthesias, hypohidrosis, and later renal and cardiac disease in a young man indicate Fabry disease, an X-linked recessive deficiency of α-galactosidase A.
